title: Does Long-Term Care Insurance Pay for Home Care? (How to Use Your Policy)
short_title: Does long-term care insurance pay for home care?
description: Did Mom or Dad buy a long-term care insurance policy years ago? It may help pay for their care at home, depending on the policy. Here's how the benefit trigger, elimination period and daily maximum work, and how Caring Companions helps you file the claim and, depending on your policy, may be able to bill the insurance company directly.
end: Find the policy. Then call us for a free review.

parts.head: Does long-term care insurance pay for home care?
parts.sub: How these policies work, and how to use one
parts.text: Did Mom or Dad buy a long-term care insurance policy years ago? It might be sitting in a drawer, and it may pay for most or all of their care at home. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's how these policies work, and how to put one to use.

parts.head: Most policies cover care at home
parts.sub: Personal care, meals, housekeeping, respite, often dementia care
parts.text: Most long-term care policies written in the last twenty-five years include care at home. That commonly covers help with bathing, dressing and toileting, meals, medication reminders and light housekeeping, respite for a family caregiver, and in many cases, dementia care.

parts.head: The benefit trigger
parts.sub: Help with 2 of 6 daily activities, or dementia
parts.text: So when does the policy start paying? Most begin once a licensed professional certifies that the person needs help with at least two of six daily activities: bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, moving from bed to chair, and continence. Or, if they have a memory problem like dementia.

parts.head: The elimination period
parts.sub: A waiting period, often 30, 60 or 90 days
parts.text: Next, the elimination period. It's a waiting period, often thirty, sixty or ninety days, when you pay for care yourself before benefits start. Think of it like a deductible, counted in days.

parts.head: Daily maximum and benefit period
parts.sub: The most it pays, and for how long
parts.text: Then there's the daily or monthly maximum, the most the policy pays, for example a hundred fifty dollars a day. And the benefit period, how long benefits last, like three years. Some policies also have inflation protection, which grows the benefit over time.

parts.head: Medicare and Medicaid are different
parts.text: A quick note. Medicare and Medicaid aren't long-term care insurance. Medicare only covers short, skilled care after a hospital stay, not ongoing help at home. Medicaid can cover long-term home care, based on income and assets. If your loved one has Missouri Medicaid, look at our sister company, Caring Companions CDS. Their number is on the screen.

parts.head: A free policy review
parts.text: Here's how we help. It starts with a free review of your policy. Call us with the policy or benefits letter handy, and we'll tell you what it covers and how billing would work, before you commit to anything.

parts.head: A call with the insurance company
parts.sub: Waiting period, daily maximum and rules, in writing
parts.text: Then we set up a call with you and the insurance company, to confirm the waiting period, the daily maximum, and the requirements, in writing.

parts.head: Assessment and claim forms
parts.text: Most insurance companies want a professional assessment and a plan of care. We help arrange it, and help you fill out and send in the claim forms, so the paperwork is right the first time.

parts.head: You choose how payment works
parts.sub: We may bill the insurer directly, or you get paid invoices
parts.text: Once the claim is approved, you choose how payment works, depending on your policy and insurer. With an assignment of benefits, we may be able to bill the insurance company directly. Or, you can pay us, and we give you paid invoices to send in for reimbursement.

parts.head: We keep the paperwork current
parts.sub: Genworth, John Hancock, Mutual of Omaha and more
parts.text: From then on, we keep the caregiver logs and paperwork current, so you're not chasing it every month. We help with policies from all the major long-term care insurers, like Genworth, John Hancock, and Mutual of Omaha.

parts.head: Find the policy
parts.sub: File cabinet, desk, or whoever helps with the finances
parts.text: So, this week, look for the policy. Check the file cabinet or the desk, or ask whoever helps with Mom or Dad's finances.
Then call us at (417) 234-8494 for a free policy review, or visit mo-care.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
